title: Redrawing the Map: How a Court Ruling Is Changing Who Wins Elections
summary: What if the lines on a map could decide who wins an election? That's exactly what's happening right now. After a big court ruling on April 29, many Southern states are quickly changing their voting maps to help Republicans win more seats in Congress. In Tennessee, lawmakers passed a new map that breaks up a district in Memphis where most voters are Black. That district was the only one in the state held by a Democrat. Now, Republicans have a good chance to win all nine of Tennessee's seats. Alabama also passed a new map, but it needs a court to say okay first. South Carolina is thinking about a map that could let Republicans win all seven seats, but some worry it might backfire. All this started when the Supreme Court said a Louisiana district drawn to have a Black majority was not allowed. This weakened a rule that protects minority voters. Louisiana even stopped its May 16 primary to draw new maps. Normally, maps are only redrawn every 10 years after the census. But last year, President Trump asked Texas to draw a map favoring Republicans, and Democrats in California did the same for their side. So far, the changes have created 14 more seats that Republicans think they can win, and 6 for Democrats. That's an 8-seat advantage for the GOP. Right now, Republicans have 217 seats and Democrats have 212. In midterm elections, the president's party usually loses seats. These new maps could make a big difference. But court fights are still going on, so nothing is final yet.
why_it_matters: When politicians redraw voting maps, they decide which voices get heard—affecting everything from how much your family pays for school lunches to how clean the air is in your neighborhood.

keywords.explanation: A district is a part of a state or city that is drawn on a map for voting in elections.
The Supreme Court is the highest court in the United States that decides if laws follow the Constitution.
A majority means more than half of a group, like having the most people in one voting district.
A primary is an election held earlier to help each party pick its candidate for the main election.
The census is a big count of all the people living in the United States, done every ten years.
Midterm elections are the elections for Congress that happen in the middle of a president's term.

background_read: In the U.S., the party in power often tries to draw voting maps that give it an advantage—a practice called gerrymandering.
The Supreme Court (the highest court) recently weakened protections for minority voters, opening the door for Southern states to reshape districts.
President Donald Trump (the U.S. president since 2025) asked Texas to redraw its map to favor Republicans, while Democrats in California did the same for their side.
Article_Structure: WHO: Republican lawmakers in Tennessee, Alabama, South Carolina, and Louisiana; the Supreme Court; and President Trump.
WHAT: They are quickly drawing new voting maps to gain seats, breaking up a Democratic district in Tennessee and overturning a Black-majority district in Louisiana.
WHY: After the Supreme Court weakened minority voting protections, Republicans see a chance to secure more seats before the midterm elections.

perspectives.description: Republican strategists say these maps correct an imbalance and give voters fairer representation in Congress.
Civil rights advocates warn that dissolving majority-Black districts silences the voices of people who already face discrimination.
Political analysts note that both Democratic and Republican-controlled states have used similar map changes to hold onto power, and the real winner is often the courts.
